description: Phase 1 plan changes of 2026-10-22, applied to the GitHub issues by the Maintenance workflow (apply-issue-updates).

T05.title: Vault open and create
T05.what: Turn a chosen folder into a vault and open existing vaults.
done: An empty folder becomes a vault with `.vaultops/` holding `config.json` (format version) and empty `pending/`, `history/`, `archive/`, `trash/`, `index/`
Reopening an existing vault changes nothing on disk, except removing leftover `.vaultops-tmp-*` files from interrupted writes
A vault with a newer format version opens read-only with a warning
`.vaultops/` never appears in the note list

T05.2.title: Choose a vault folder
T05.2.what: Let the user pick a folder with the system folder picker, using the official Tauri `dialog` plugin (approved).
done: Picking a folder opens or creates the vault
Cancelling the picker changes nothing

T08.title: Trash
T08.what: Delete moves a note to `.vaultops/trash/<timestamp>/<original relative path>`: the folder name holds the deletion time and the inner path holds where it came from, so no separate record is needed. Restore puts it back; delete forever only from Trash.
done: Delete, restore, restore into a missing folder (goes to the vault root), restore with a name clash (" 2", including a capital-letter-only clash)
No code path erases a note outside Trash
Trash is never emptied automatically

T08.2.title: Delete to trash, restore, delete forever
T08.2.what: Implement delete, restore and delete forever on the Host using the trash layout above.
done: All T08 acceptance tests pass on the fake host and the real host
Delete forever asks for confirmation

T09.title: Editor setup and block ids
T09.what: Tiptap editor with a permanent id on every block-level node.
done: Block types: paragraph, heading 1 and 2, bullet list, numbered list, flat task (checkbox only), code, quote; inline: text marks, links, date chip
Only these block types in this phase (tables come before the first public release)
A schema test fails when any block node type lacks an id
Duplicate ids are replaced on load

T09.1.title: Add the editor and the block schema with ids
T09.1.what: Add Tiptap (approved) with its UniqueID extension covering a single `BLOCK_TYPES` list. Use stock Tiptap extensions wherever they exist.
done: Schema test over `BLOCK_TYPES`
Load with duplicate ids gives unique ids

T09.2.title: Flat task block, text marks and inline date chip
T09.2.what: A task block holding inline text and a checkbox (stock Tiptap task item where it fits); the standard text marks (bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code); an inline date node with no id. Builds on T09.1.
done: Task toggles and survives save and reload
Each mark survives save and reload
Date chip has no id and survives save and reload

T12.title: Slash menu
T12.what: `/` at the start of a block or after a space opens a 9-item menu, built on Tiptap's `Suggestion` utility.
done: Items: paragraph, heading 1, heading 2, bullet, numbered, task, code, quote, inline date
Opens in both positions, not mid-word
Each item inserts the right block with an id
No other items, including no separate "task list" item (several tasks in a row are a list)
A "Link to note" entry is added once note links (T22) exist

T14.title: Pull an item out of a list
T14.what: Converting a list item pulls it out as its own block and splits the list in two.
done: Allowed targets: text, heading, task
Item ids kept; one undo step
Tests: first, middle, last and only item; nested items; undo restores the original list
A list shows as one block on screen while each item keeps its own id in the file

T15.title: Nesting rule
T15.what: Nothing nests inside a list item or quote beyond what the editor already allows.
done: Each disallowed nesting is refused through paste, conversion and drag
Nested list items, and paragraphs inside list items and quotes, still work

T17.title: Drag handle and moving blocks within a note
T17.what: Hover handle beside a block with a "Turn into" menu; drag reorders blocks.
done: Reorder keeps ids
Paste of 18 blocks gives 18 unique ids
Real mouse drag in a headless browser and on macOS

T17.1.title: Drag handle and "Turn into" menu
T17.1.what: Handle shows beside the hovered block, using Tiptap's drag-handle extension; its click menu offers "Turn into".
done: Handle appears beside the hovered block
Menu runs conversions through T13

T19.title: Note view and basic app shell
T19.what: The main window: sidebar plus note view with a title field and the editor.
done: Create, edit, quit, reopen: the edit is there
New note command
The last vault reopens at launch
Window size and position are remembered, using the official Tauri `window-state` plugin (approved)

T22.1.title: Link node and picker
T22.1.what: Note links use Tiptap's `Mention` node with the target's `noteId` as its id; the picker reuses the slash menu's `Suggestion` setup, opened by a keyboard shortcut and a "Link to note" slash entry.
done: Pick and insert
Slash entry added to the menu

T23.title: Backlinks
T23.what: A backlinks panel (note links only), computed in memory when the vault opens and kept up to date while it is open. No saved index in this phase; `.vaultops/index/` stays reserved.
done: Backlinks are correct after opening a vault, adding a link, removing a link, renaming and trashing a note
Nothing is written to `.vaultops/index/`

T23.1.title: Backlink map in memory
T23.1.what: Build a map of which notes link to which, from the notes scanned on open; update it on save, rename and trash.
done: Map equals a fresh scan after each change
Opening a vault with many notes stays within the T27 performance budget

T27.title: Performance: many cards and large notes
T27.what: Measure on macOS: open time, memory and typing delay with 10, 50 and 100 cards; a 1,000-block note; a 100,000-character block; autosave on both. (Merged from T30.)
done: Numbers reported for each case, measured as keystroke-to-paint and open-to-first-paint time
Single-note target: under about 50 ms to paint and under 500 ms to open, or follow-up issues filed
Maintainer sets the many-card pass line from the numbers

T28.title: Core invariant tests and broken-file fixtures
T28.what: One test per rule that protects future version history: permanent block ids; ordered block list; notes tracked by `noteId`; `.vaultops/` reserved; a format version in every file. Plus fixture files: corrupt line, missing id, duplicate id, newer format version, truncated file, unknown block type, and awkward titles (`a/b`, a leading dot, a 500-character title, a capital-letter-only clash). (Merged from T29.1.)
done: Each invariant test fails against a deliberately broken version of the rule
Automated tests load each fixture without crashing or writing

T31.title: macOS walk-through
T31.what: Full manual pass on the real macOS app.
done: Create, edit, convert, drag, save, quit, reopen; delete and restore; paste; conversion menus; properties and tags; capital-letter-only rename; cross-card move; native file drops
Walk each broken-file fixture from T28 in the real app (merged from T29.2); the checklist is committed
The pass is run with the network off and no account
Written report lists every step as passed, failed or not tested
